_note: Task 5's register of the state itself: confidence, corruption, the courts, the press, the administration and the settlement of the streets. The institution group prices its work on the only verdict the register carries -- overall approval -- because a state reform that leaves no trace in the country's confidence is indistinguishable from one that never happened. The schema-wide notes (_field_note, _progress_note, _pulse_note) live once in economy.json; this file carries only what is this group's own. Entries gated by terms_served or by unrest carry their gate in `possible`, so the offer itself is what makes the goal honest.

programme.name: A Governing Majority of Opinion
programme.summary: Fifty-five per cent, and the register holds you to the number -- a governing majority in the [g=poll]polls[/g], where every other [g=programme]programme[/g] this term will have to be paid for. The fail line is the forties: an opinion the country has withdrawn.

programme.name: Clean Hands
programme.summary: An anti-corruption drive filed as the term's institutional work and priced on the only verdict that matters: the country's confidence. The agency is created on the day the [g=programme]programme[/g] is chosen; the judgement waits for the number.

programme.name: Settling the Streets
programme.summary: Offerable only once the country is actually angry, and concluded only when it is not: unrest back under the line the offer was written at. A settlement is the instrument; the register is the witness.

programme.name: The Free Airwaves
programme.summary: A broadcasting law the government cannot quiet, judged like everything else this term -- on the confidence it leaves behind. The press freedom is granted on the day of the choice; the verdict belongs to the register.

programme.name: The Sworn Offices
programme.summary: The courts settled beyond a government's reach, and a [g=programme]programme[/g] for a second mandate only -- a first-term president who promises judicial independence is announcing a fight, not a programme.

programme.name: The Long Record
programme.summary: Fifty-eight per cent in a second mandate -- the number a re-elected president is promised by the job and rarely shown by the country. Open-ended, because a record compounds or it does not; the reward is drawn from every bloc because a number that size is made of every bloc.

programme.name: The Civil Register
programme.summary: The administration rewritten onto one register -- licences, filings and the wait for both, halved. Ten months on the clock, because an administration that cannot be fixed inside a year was never going to be fixed.
